correctness.rationale: Directly reconstruct the observed Markov operator: \(Ph_0=p h_1\) and \(Ph_j=p h_{j+1}+(1-p)h_{j-1}\) for \(j\ge1\) because the inverse-digit average annihilates h_0. Lebesgue independence makes digit levels orthogonal, so the time-covariance counts Dyck returns and equals sigma^2 Catalan_m [p(1-p)]^m at lag 2m and zero at odd lags. Pair summation proves finite variance, summability and Catalan generating function yield Gamma, and Stirling estimates prove the \(8\sqrt{2/\pi}\) critical finite-size coefficient with O(1) remainder. For p!=1/2 differentiating the generating series gives the stated finite-size intercept. These arguments prove all \(b\ge2\), all \(p\in(0,1)\), any nonconstant digit coding, and every integer time; independent finite-prefix rational calculations check sample instances but are not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The originating dynamical system is studied specifically for its Lyapunov sign transition, yet uniform one-point marginals conceal changing temporal dependencies. The new exact covariance identifies a Catalan \(n^{-3/2}\) critical tail, strict even/odd temporal structure, unique factor-three maximal integrated variance at the neutral threshold, and the precise square-root finite-size defect versus the bounded off-critical correction. These quantitatively distinguish critical observations, not merely a renamed textbook identity. The half-line Catalan path representation is structurally forced by the specified random maps and applies simultaneously to every nontrivial leading-digit coding.
